title: Vacancy Provisions Schedule, LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy
content:
The LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy treats a rental building with no tenant in residence as vacant. This schedule gives, tier by tier, the vacancy figures the policy works with: the exclusion period, the settlement reduction, whether a vacancy permit can be added and on what terms, and the vacancy period after which the carrier may cancel.

## Schedule

| | DP-1 Basic | DP-2 Broad | DP-3 Special | DP-3 Special Plus | DP-3 Premier | DP-3 Portfolio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vacancy exclusion period (consecutive calendar days vacant) | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |
| Reduction of other covered losses while vacant beyond that period without a permit (percent) | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 |
| Vacancy permit available | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Longest vacancy permit (calendar days) | 0 | 90 | 90 | 120 | 180 | 180 |
| Vacancy permit rate (percent of the annual term premium, prorated over the permit days) | 0 | 25 | 25 | 20 | 20 | 15 |
| Consecutive days vacant without a permit after which the carrier cancels for a substantial change in risk (calendar days) | 90 | 90 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 180 |

## Reading the schedule

- After 60 consecutive days of vacancy, vandalism and glass breakage are excluded and other losses are reduced by 15 percent, on every tier, unless a vacancy permit covers the date.
- LandlordGuard DP-1 Basic offers no vacancy permit; its longest permit and permit rate are therefore 0.
- The vacancy permit rate is a percentage of the annual term premium, prorated over the permit days.

## Basis Q&A

**Which tiers allow the longest permits?** LandlordGuard DP-3 Premier and DP-3 Portfolio, at 180 days each; DP-3 Special Plus allows 120 days; DP-2 Broad and DP-3 Special allow 90 days.

**On which tier does the carrier wait longest before cancelling for vacancy?** LandlordGuard DP-3 Portfolio, at 180 days; DP-1 Basic and DP-2 Broad use 90 days and the other DP-3 tiers 120 days.
